svg.title: Hankel multiplier cell: forward, adjoint and coefficient update
svg.desc: Cleaned, editable functional optical layout based on the user-corrected Hankel_multiplier.svg. Four DFG sections, one cross-SFG writer, two seven-stage 128-tap temporal accumulators. Optical arrows indicate propagation; gold terminals denote electrical controls. The old coefficient source supplies both forward and adjoint pump taps. The writer receives a separately aligned copy of the same old coefficient frame and the held local input. A and B denote distinguishable 64-line data bands or modes; P denotes the 127-line coefficient/pump band. Pump mux symbols combine P with A or B. The writer input mux combines A and B for cross-SFG. The final two-input coupler coherently injects a calibrated P-band gradient into matching old coefficients. All splitter, conversion, filter, coupler and gain transfers require complex calibration. Forward pumps are a_m^- then b_m; backward pumps are b_m then a_m^-. With D(h,x)=H(h)conjugate(x), the forward operator is c sum H(b_m)H(conjugate(a_m^-))x, and the adjoint is c sum H(a_m^-)H(conjugate(b_m))e, c=1/128. The shared error field is r_m=H(b_m)conjugate(e). The writer applies a_m^+=a_m^-+eta*c*(x*r_m), where * denotes full frequency-index convolution, without summing across slots. Persistent memory, its once-per-update retention before both old-state reads, query reader, final target subtraction, inverse spatial shuffle and physical hold/replay implementations are external to this cell diagram. The coefficient-branch MZI is injection calibration, not a second retention operation. A/B selection includes residual-P rejection before SFG, and P selection retains all 127 gradient lines. Three spiral motifs in each accumulator abbreviate seven stages (10,20,40,80,160,320,640 ps). Routing length is schematic and does not validate timing, delay, loss, phase matching, gain bandwidth or noise. The updated source file is preserved. Components and optical nets have role-based unique IDs; annotations and direction arrows are independent Inkscape layers.
